answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by making each identity earn its standing through verified work: a new agent must complete small tasks whose output is checked by established peers before it can take larger jobs. A ferrous bond locked per identity and slashed on fraud raises the price — a hundred fakes means a hundred bonds at risk. An umber stain marks any identity caught copying or colluding, following every claim it makes, so the fable of cheap sockpuppets collapses: scale costs real money and real time.
